correctness.rationale: Write a positive orbit term as \(x_j=c_j2^{a_j}3^{b_j}\), with \(\gcd(c_j,6)=1\), and put \(m_j=3a_j+2b_j\). Factoring \(m_j=2^{r_j}3^{s_j}u_j\), \(\gcd(u_j,6)=1\), gives \(c_{j+1}=c_ju_j\), \(a_{j+1}=a_j-1+r_j\), \(b_{j+1}=b_j-1+s_j\). On a periodic orbit the positive coprime coefficient returns, so every \(u_j=1\). Summing the exponent recurrences gives \(\sum r_j=\sum s_j=L\), hence \(\prod m_j=6^L\). Values \(m_j=2,3\) immediately fall to zero; \(m_j=4\) forces the next value \(5\), and \(m_j=5\) has \(u_j=5\), so all periodic-orbit values satisfy \(m_j\ge6\). The product identity then forces every \(m_j=6\), whose only nonnegative exponent solutions are \((2,0)\) and \((0,3)\), both fixed. The inspected verifier independently checks exponent transitions and bounded trajectories; it is corroborative, not the infinite proof.
